notes: «شَكَا هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ» is the complaint opening (rule 5): the asker transmits, the Imam answers and is the last link.
«قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَاشِدٍ وَ كُنْتُ دَائِمَ اَلْعِلَّةِ» is Muhammad b. Rashid's own account added after the answer; it is not written as a link here.
«شَكَا هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ» is the complaint opening (rule 5): the asker transmits, the Imam answers and is the last link.
«قَالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ رَاشِدٍ وَ كُنْتُ دَائِمَ اَلْعِلَّةِ» is Muhammad b. Rashid's own account added after the answer; it is not written as a link here.
«وَ شَكَا هِشَامُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ» : the complainer transmits the answer, and the Imam he complains to is the last link (rule 5, «شكا»).
«قال ففعلت ذلك» (Hisham's words) and «قال محمد بن راشد وكنت دائم العلة» (Ibn Rashid's own story) are inside the report, not routes.
